papers.version_note: arXiv:2604.05422v1 (quant-ph, 7 Apr 2026): main text (pages 1 to 18, references included) followed by the Supplementary Information (13 pages). One copy of the paper only.
papers.what_it_is: An experimental and theoretical paper from the Stevens Institute of Technology group that links two SPDC waveguides on a thin-film lithium niobate chip through a lossy chromium-loaded third waveguide (an anti-PT dissipative coupling) and reports phase-tunable two-, three- and four-photon correlations.

assertions.value: The authors claim to demonstrate, for the first time, multi-photon interference in the anti-PT regime.
quotes: demonstrate, for the first time, multi-photon interference in the anti-PT regime
assertions.certainty_reason: A priority claim made by the authors without a literature comparison in the paper.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper cites two-photon PT-symmetric interference experiments (refs 33 to 36) but gives no systematic survey that would support the word first.

assertions.value: The authors describe a chip fabricated on a z-cut, 600-nm TFLN wafer with two periodically poled lithium niobate (PPLN) waveguides (4 mm length), carrying modes a and b, and a central waveguide, carrying mode c, engineered to exhibit a high propagation loss.
quotes: The chip device is fabricated on a z-cut, 600-nm TFLN wafer.
two periodically poled lithium niobate (PPLN) waveguides (4 mm length), with propagating modes a and b and a central waveguide, with mode c, engineered to exhibit a high propagation loss.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own device structure in Section 2.
assertions.reader_inference: The Fig. 1 caption says the structure consists of three periodically poled waveguides, while the text says only a and b are PPLN; the caption and text differ in wording.

assertions.value: The authors state that the dissipation of mode c, characterized by a propagation loss rate γ, is introduced by a chromium (Cr) strip deposited above the middle waveguide.
quotes: The dissipation of mode c, characterized by a propagation loss rate γ, is introduced by a chromium (Cr) strip deposited above the middle waveguide.
The loss reservoir is realized by depositing a chromium (Cr) strip on top of the middle waveguide.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states how the loss reservoir is built.

assertions.value: The authors report the cross-section design parameters waveguide top width w1 = 1.37 µm, waveguide height h1 = 348 nm, Cr width w2 = 250 nm and inter-waveguide gap w3 = 600 nm, and a poling period of 3.25 µm for waveguides of 4 mm length; the quasi-phase-matching design used simulated effective indices n775 = 2.1262 and n1550 = 1.8875.
assertions.anchor: Fig. 1 caption, p.3; Supplementary S1, p.1
quotes: Design parameters: waveguide top width w1 = 1.37 µm, waveguide height h1 = 348 nm, Cr width w2 = 250 nm, inter-waveguide gap w3 = 600 nm
each with a length of 4 mm and a poling period 3.25 µm
The solution yields effective refractive indices of n775 = 2.1262 and n1550 = 1.8875.
The corresponding QPM poling period is therefore Λ = 3.25 µm.

assertions.reader_inference: The Methods section uses slightly different indices (n_omega 1.8926 and n_2omega 2.1265) for the nonlinear coefficient than Supplementary S1 (1.8875 and 2.1262); the paper does not comment on the difference.

assertions.value: The authors report that ferroelectric domain inversion was achieved by applying 60 cycles of 480-V high-voltage pulses to the electrodes, and that the Cr metal strip (250-nm wide, 20-nm thick) was fabricated on the 100-nm SiO2 cladding layer, aligned directly above the central waveguides.

the Cr metal strip (250-nm wide, 20-nm thick) was fabricated on the 100-nm SiO2 cladding layer, aligned directly above the central waveguides

assertions.value: The authors state that the nonlinear Hamiltonian describes SPDC generating non-degenerate signal-idler photon pairs in waveguides a and b, and that the nonlinear terms in waveguide c are neglected because the pump field strength in waveguide c is assumed approximately zero due to weak coupling, so the modes c originate from linear hopping of photons generated in a or b.
quotes: HNL describes the nonlinear SPDC process that generates non-degenerate signal-idler photon pairs in the two waveguides a and b
assuming the pump field strength ϵc ≈ 0 in waveguide c due to weak coupling
Thus the modes cs,i in HL are not generated locally in waveguide c via SPDC, but originate from linear hopping
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states the scope of its model in Section 2.

assertions.value: The authors state that the adiabatic elimination of the lossy intermediate modes can be performed under the condition γ ≫ |κs,i|, which reduces the three modes to two with a non-Hermitian effective Hamiltonian and an effective coupling strength Γ = |κ|2/γ (the square of the magnitude of κ divided by γ; the exponent was printed flat).
quotes: The adiabatic elimination of the lossy intermediate modes cs and ci can be performed independently
under the condition γ ≫ |κs,i|.
with an effective coupling strength Γ = |κ|2/γ.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper defines its effective coupling and states the validity condition of the elimination in Section 2.
assertions.reader_inference: From the Supplementary S1 values the ratio of gamma at 1550 nm (813 per cm) to kappa at 1550 nm (about 76.6 per cm, from pi over twice the 205 µm beating length) is about 10.6, so the condition is met by roughly one order of magnitude, not by a large margin (reader arithmetic).

assertions.value: The authors state that the reduced linear coupling terms of the effective Hamiltonian possess anti-PT symmetry, satisfying the anticommutation relation of the PT operator with the reduced linear Hamiltonian, and that for Γ ≫ gϵ the nonlinear SPDC process can be treated as a perturbation to the anti-PT system.
quotes: possess anti-PT symmetry, satisfying {P T, HL′ } = 0.
For Γ ≫ gϵ, the nonlinear SPDC process described
by HNL can be treated as a perturbation to the anti-PT system.
assertions.certainty_reason: The property follows from the stated effective Hamiltonian; the regime condition is quoted with it.

assertions.value: The authors compare the anti-PT linked system to a reference in which two PPLN waveguides are coupled coherently, described by a coupled-mode Hamiltonian given in the paper.
quotes: we compare the above anti-PT linked system to a coherent,
Specifically, we consider two PPLN waveguides coupled coherently, described
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper defines its comparison system.
assertions.reader_inference: This coherent reference is a simulated model only; no coherently coupled chip is reported.

assertions.value: The authors simulate the dynamics with a Lindblad master equation and with a non-Hermitian effective Hamiltonian, and state that the fundamental difference between the two approaches lies in the quantum jump terms, which are neglected in the effective Hamiltonian method; the quantum jump term describes the state update induced by continuous monitoring from the environment.
quotes: This reformulation demonstrates that the fundamental difference between the two approaches
which are neglected in the effective Hamiltonian method.
term (quantum jumps) of the dissipator describes the state update induced by continuous monitoring from the
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper defines the two simulation methods and the term that separates them.

assertions.value: The authors report that their simulations use gϵ = 6.93 m−1 and Γ = 7.22 cm−1 with a Fock basis truncation of Nmax = 10.
quotes: We utilize the parameters gϵ = 6.93 m−1 and Γ = 7.22 cm−1, applying a Fock
basis truncation of mµ, nµ ≤ Nmax where Nmax = 10.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states the parameters of its own simulation.
assertions.reader_inference: Gamma of 7.22 per cm is 722 per metre, about 104 times gϵ of 6.93 per metre (reader arithmetic), consistent with the condition for the perturbative regime.

inter-pair correlation ratio which is simply g(4)/ga(2)gb(2).
yielding a baseline of R(4) = 1.

assertions.value: The authors report from simulation that in the Hermitian coherent system the mean photon number and G(4) oscillate because coherent coupling disrupts phase matching, whereas in the anti-PT system the phase matching remains undisturbed because the bright modes decay and the dark modes remain lossless, so both the mean photon number and G(4) accumulate monotonically regardless of the relative phase, under the condition that decay rates dominate coherent coupling coefficients.
assertions.anchor: Fig. 3 and Section 2, p.6 to p.7
quotes: coherent coupling disrupts phase matching in the PPLN waveguides, and the additional propagation phases induce oscillatory behavior in the evolution.
In the anti-PT symmetry system, phase matching remains undisturbed because the bright modes are governed by dissipative evolution
and the dark modes remain lossless, with the condition that decay rates dominate coherent coupling coefficients
As a result, both the mean photon number and G(4) accumulate monotonically during propagation, regardless of the relative phase.
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical simulation of one parameter set with a physical argument; plots are not in the text layer.

assertions.value: The paper states that in the bright/dark basis the dark mode operators vanish entirely from the dissipative term of the master equation, so the loss acts exclusively on the bright state and the dark state remains transparent to dissipation, residing in a Decoherence-Free Subspace.
quotes: Notably, the dark mode operators Dµ vanish entirely from the dissipative term, revealing the selective nature of the loss channel.
The loss exclusively acts on the bright state, whereas the dark state remains transparent to dissipation, residing in a Decoherence-Free Subspace (DFS) [4].
assertions.certainty_reason: An algebraic consequence of the stated master equation in the bright/dark basis (Eq. 13), quoted with its statement.

assertions.value: The authors state that the dark-state decoherence-free subspace is an exact DFS of the dissipator but not a strict DFS of the full Liouvillian, and that the collective dissipation continuously removes bright components, leading to dissipative purification toward the dark manifold as a global attractor.
quotes: Note this is an exact DFS of the dissipator, but not a strict DFS of the full Liouvillian.
The collective dissipation continuously removes bright components, leading to dissipative purification toward the dark manifold as a global attractor.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state the limit of their DFS statement in Section 2.
assertions.reader_inference: The nonlinear SPDC term couples bright and dark modes at nonzero relative phase, which is why the DFS is not strict for the full Liouvillian (reader reading of Eq. 12).

assertions.value: The authors state, from the mean photon number equations of motion, that the bright photon experiences dissipation at a rate of 4Γ, while the dark photon remains protected and therefore exhibits a significantly longer lifetime, given the condition Γ ≫ gϵ.
quotes: As indicated by Eqs. (14)–(17), the bright photon experiences dissipation at a rate of
4Γ, while the dark photon remains protected and therefore exhibits a significantly longer lifetime, given the
condition Γ ≫ gϵ.
assertions.certainty_reason: Derived from the stated master equation, with the regime condition quoted.

assertions.value: The authors claim that the dissipative structure provides a robust anti-PT protection mechanism against disorder, because scattering into the bright subspace caused by fabrication imperfections is immediately suppressed by the Cr strip, biasing the dynamics toward the protected dark manifold, and that the effect is essential for creating error-resilient and DFS-based quantum light sources.
quotes: The dissipative structure provides a robust anti-PT protection mechanism against disorder:
any resulting scattering into the bright subspace is immediately suppressed by the Cr strip, thereby biasing the dynamics toward the protected dark manifold.
the effect is essential for creating error-resilient and DFS-based quantum light sources
assertions.certainty_reason: An author claim; the paper reports no disorder simulation or measurement of robustness.
assertions.reader_inference: No simulation with fabrication disorder, and no experiment varying it, appears in the text; the claim rests on the qualitative argument.

assertions.value: The authors report that the master-equation and non-Hermitian-Hamiltonian approaches give identical G(4) dynamics in the anti-PT system, while the mean photon number differs between them for nonzero relative phases because quantum-jump terms are included in the master equation but absent in the NHH description.
quotes: The master-equation and NHH approaches yield identical G(4) dynamics, while ⟨n⟩ exhibits discrepancies between the two approaches
because quantum-jump terms are included in the master equation but absent in the NHH description.
there is a discrepancy between the two approaches in the mean photon number for non-zero relative phases.
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical simulation result for one parameter set.

assertions.value: The authors state that the master equation approach is required to give the fully accurate dynamics of the normalized correlation g(4)(z), while for the inter-pair correlation ratio R(4) the non-Hermitian Hamiltonian approach remains a sufficient approximation, because R(4) depends only on unnormalized four- and two-photon correlations.
assertions.anchor: Section 2, p.7; Supplementary S3, p.9 to p.10
quotes: the master equation approach is required to provide the fully accurate dynamics of the normalized correlation g(4)(z)
for the inter-pair correlation ratio R(4), the non-Hermitian Hamiltonian approach remains a sufficient approximation.
In contrast, the ratio R(4), which depends only on the unnormalized four- and two-photon correlations, is largely unaffected
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical comparison (Fig. S4) with an explanation; no bound is proved.

assertions.value: The authors explain that quantum jumps leave single dark photons from broken pairs, giving an unequal population of bright and dark states at θ = π, and that the effective-Hamiltonian approach excludes these noise photons from the mean photon number, so the denominator of g(4) is underestimated and the approach yields a higher unphysical correlation than the master equation; the master-equation g(4) shows a minimum at θ = π and the NHH result a maximum.
assertions.anchor: Supplementary S3, Fig. S5, p.10 to p.11
quotes: This accumulation of unpaired photons results in an unequal population of Bright and Dark states at θ = π, as shown in Fig. S5(c).
Because the single Dark photons from broken pairs—which constitute noise—are excluded from the mean photon number in the effective Hamiltonian calculation, the denominator of g(4) is underestimated.
Consequently, this approach yields a higher unphysical correlation value compared to the master equation.
at θ = π, the master-equation result shows a minimum, whereas the NHH result shows a maximum.
assertions.certainty_reason: Explanatory argument supported by simulated figures; no formal derivation is given.

assertions.value: The authors report that the measured normalized fourth-order correlation g(4), normalized to its maximum, reaches a minimum at θ = π, which they state confirms the theoretical prediction of the quantum jump effect.
quotes: The g(4) reaches a minimum at θ = π, confirming the theoretical prediction of the quantum jump effect.
Experimental data and theory are normalized to their peak values.
assertions.certainty_reason: One experimental phase sweep, reported only as a normalized curve.
assertions.reader_inference: Because data and theory are each normalized to their peak, the absolute g(4) values are not given in the text, and the figure cannot rule out other mean-photon-number effects.

assertions.value: The authors report an optimal operating temperature of 69 °C, which maximizes the SHG output power at the QPM wavelength, reaching 30 nW after Cr absorption.
quotes: We determined the optimal operating temperature to be 69 °C, which maximizes the SHG output power at the QPM wavelength (reaching 30 nW after Cr absorption).
assertions.certainty_reason: A single device characterization.

assertions.value: The authors state that a CW pump laser at 775.4 nm, with its polarization tuned by an FPC, is launched into the chip through the FWDM, and that the chip temperature is maintained at 69 °C by a thermoelectric cooler with a stability of ±3 mK.
quotes: a CW pump laser at 775.4 nm, with its polarization tuned by an FPC, is launched into the chip through the FWDM.
The chip temperature is maintained at 69 °C by a thermoelectric cooler (TEC) with a stability of ±3 mK.

assertions.value: The authors report two cascaded long-pass filters per output path with a total of 140-dB pump attenuation, two cascaded DWDM filters (125-GHz bandwidth) centred at 1549.35 nm and 1552.54 nm to separate signal and idler, and SNSPDs with a detection efficiency of 85% and a dark count of 50-100 Hz.

assertions.value: The authors state that the comparison shown in the R(4) figure is a numerical prediction for a Hermitian coherent-coupling system with the same propagation length (4 mm) as the experimental anti-PT chip.

For an on-chip pump power P2ω(0) = 4 × 10−3 W, this yields ϵ = 6.41 × 10−10 J1/2.

assertions.value: The authors define an experimental normalized four-photon correlation from the four-photon coincidence counts divided by the product of the four single count rates, the total integration time and the three coincidence-window widths, and state that T = 30 min is the total integration time.

assertions.value: The authors report from mode-solver simulations a beating length Lbeat = 205 µm, a hopping rate κ775 = 3.14 cm−1 for 775-nm light, dissipation rates γ1550 = 813 cm−1 and γ775 = 14 cm−1, and an effective coupling strength Γ = |κ|2/γ = 7.22 cm−1.
quotes: The beating length is Lbeat = 205 µm
we obtain the hopping rate of κ775 = 3.14 cm−1 for 775-nm light.
we find γ1550 = 813 cm−1 and γ775 = 14 cm−1.
The effective coupling strength is Γ = |κ|2/γ = 7.22 cm−1.

assertions.reader_inference: The hopping rate at 1550 nm follows as pi over twice 205 µm, about 76.6 per cm, and (76.6)^2 / 813 gives about 7.22 per cm, matching the stated Γ (reader arithmetic); the paper gives no measured gamma or kappa.

assertions.value: The authors state that the weak coupling condition for 775-nm light, κ1550 ≫ κ775, ensures that the pump coupled into waveguide c is negligible.
quotes: The weak coupling condition for 775-nm light, κ1550 ≫ κ775, ensures that the pump coupled into waveguide c is negligible (ϵc ≈ 0)
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states the condition that scopes its model of the pump.
assertions.reader_inference: Supplementary S4 states that adiabatic elimination does not hold for the pump (see the separate assertion), so the pump in waveguide c is negligible only by this weak-coupling argument.

assertions.value: The authors assume the effective detuning between the two identical waveguides a and b to be approximately zero and state that, with the effective coupling larger than the detuning, the four-photon correlation is investigated in the anti-PT symmetry unbroken regime.
quotes: we assume the effective detuning ∆ = (ka − kb)/2 ≈ 0.
the four-photon correlation is investigated in Anti-PT symmetry unbroken regime.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states the regime its analysis assumes.
assertions.reader_inference: The detuning is assumed from the designed identity of the waveguides; no measured value is given.

Experimental verification of equal power splitting, a signature of operation in the anti-PT system.

assertions.value: The authors report optimized one-input two-output MMI splitter dimensions of coupler length LMMI = 34 µm and taper length Lt = 10 µm for the Mach-Zehnder interferometer.
quotes: the resulting optimal values are LMMI = 34 µm and Lt = 10 µm.

assertions.value: The authors derive, for the Hermitian coherent system at relative phase π (coefficients Λco = 0 and Λx = −gϵ), a mean photon number ⟨n(z)⟩ = sinh2(gϵz) and G(4)(z) = S4C4 + 2S6C2 + S8 = sinh4(gϵz) cosh2(2gϵz) (exponents printed flat), growing monotonically.
quotes: For the coherent system at phase θ = π, the coefficients reduce to Λco = 0 and Λx = −gϵ.
⟨n(z)⟩ = sinh2(gϵz)
G(4)(z) = S4C4 + 2S6C2 + S8 = sinh4(gϵz) cosh2(2gϵz).
assertions.certainty_reason: An analytic result with its phase condition quoted; checked against simulation in Fig. S3(b).
assertions.reader_inference: The identity S4C4 + 2S6C2 + S8 = sinh4 times cosh2(2x) checks out algebraically (reader check); the word monotonically in the value is the reader's reading of the closed form.

assertions.value: The authors state that, because of algebraic complexity, they compute the anti-PT four-photon correlation with a semi-analytical approach that uses the analytic operator solutions and assumes the state remains Gaussian throughout propagation, and report excellent agreement with the full numerical simulations in the supplementary figure comparing them.
quotes: Due to the algebraic complexity of expanding the full four-photon correlation into a single explicit formula, we adopt a semi-analytical approach.
assuming that the state remains Gaussian throughout propagation.
Fig. S3(a) demonstrates excellent agreement between the semi-analytical results and full numerical simulations.
Numerical and analytical results agree well in both cases.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states the approximation (Gaussian state) under which the anti-PT G(4) is evaluated.

assertions.value: The authors report a phase-conversion coefficient b = 0.037 rad/mW and an initial phase θ0 = 0.56 rad from fitting the classical pump output powers of waveguides a and b measured as the heater power was increased from 0 to 242 mW; these parameters map heater power to phase in all phase-tuning measurements.
quotes: Fitting the measured data yields a phase-conversion coefficient b = 0.037 rad/mW and the initial phase θ0 = 0.56 rad.
The classical output powers Pa and Pb from waveguides a and b are measured as the heater power is increased from 0 to 242 mW.
assertions.certainty_reason: A single calibration fit; the fit quality is in the figure only.
assertions.reader_inference: Every phase value in the experimental figures rests on this calibration from classical pump light.

assertions.value: The authors state that the condition for adiabatic elimination of the pump (γ775 ≫ κ775) is not met, so the system functions approximately as three evanescently coupled waveguides for the classical pump light; instead of equal output powers, the pump outputs show complementary phase tuning curves.
quotes: Since the condition for adiabatic elimination of the pump (γ775 ≫ κ775) is not met
the system functions approximately as three evanescently coupled waveguides for the classical pump light.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state this limit of the pump model in Supplementary S4.
assertions.reader_inference: The stated values gamma 14 per cm and kappa 3.14 per cm at 775 nm give a ratio of about 4.5 (reader arithmetic), consistent with the condition not being met.

assertions.value: The authors conclude that, by linking two SPDC processes through coupling to a common lossy reservoir, they created exotic quantum states among two, three, and four photons, and that decoherence, rather than causing loss of quantum information, serves as a resource to robustly create the quantum correlation.
quotes: By linking two SPDC processes through their coupling to a common lossy reservoir, we have created exotic quantum states amongst two, three, and four photons.
In this paradigm, the decoherence, rather than causing loss of quantum information, serves as a resource to robustly create the quantum correlation.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own conclusion from coincidence-count phase tuning.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper reports coincidence-to-accidental ratios and fringe visibilities but no state tomography, entanglement witness or Bell-type test, so entanglement of the generated states is not demonstrated in the text.

assertions.value: The authors state that the robustness lends the approach to generation of quantum correlated and entangled states over even higher photon numbers.
quotes: This robustness lends our approach to generation of quantum correlated and entangled states over even higher photon numbers.
assertions.certainty_reason: A forward-looking claim without evidence in the paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that most experimental studies thus far have used classical systems to realize effective Hamiltonians with PT or anti-PT symmetry, and that only recently have the effects of PT symmetry in second quantization been experimentally studied through two-photon quantum interference (references 33 to 36).
quotes: most experimental studies thus far have used classical systems to realize effective Hamiltonians with PT or anti-PT symmetry.
Only recently, the effects of PT symmetry in second quantization have been experimentally studied through two-photon quantum interference [33–36]
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' summary of the literature, attributed to other work.
